newsitem.title: USA: USDA to hold June 24 meeting on meat inspection.
newsitem.headline: USDA to hold June 24 meeting on meat inspection.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) Tuesday said it would hold a meeting June 24 on its role in the wake of the implementation of new federal meat inspection rules.
"Every aspect of traditional FSIS methods of inspection for slaughter and processing needs to be reconsidered," the agency said in notice in the Federal Register.

"All methods are subject to change as long as the agency can fulfill its responsibilities to ensure that the industries produce safe, wholesome, unadulterated and properly labeled meat and poultry products," FSIS said.
It said it was also considering adding methods to better ensure food safety and other consumer protections in distribution channels.
The day-long meeting will be held in Arlington, Va.

The first phase of revolutionary new meat inspection rules, which require slaughter and processing plants to do scientific testing for disease-causing bacteria, took effect in January. The rules are modeled on the food safety principle, Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP).

Previously, goverment inspectors relied on sight and smell to certify meat and poultry was safe to eat, a system little changed since Upton Sinclair's expose on the Chicago stockyards, "The Jungle," led to the enactment of the Federal Meat Inspection Act in 1907.
